Privacy Policy — Notebook

Last updated: 25 August 2026

The short version

Notebook keeps everything you write on your own device. It has no account, no

sign-in, and no server. Nothing you write is sent to me or to anyone else.

What Notebook stores

Everything you type — your entries, their dates, the notebooks you sort them

into, and your settings for theme, handwriting and text size — is saved in a

single file on your device.

That file never leaves your phone except through Apple's own backup, described

below.

What Notebook does not do

Notebook has no code that connects to the internet. It does not:

  • create an account or ask you to sign in
  • send your writing anywhere
  • use analytics, tracking, or advertising
  • collect crash reports or usage statistics
  • ask for the camera, microphone, location, photos or contacts

The fonts the app uses are included inside the app itself. Nothing is

downloaded while you use it.

Backups

If you have iPhone backups turned on, iOS includes Notebook's file in your

backup, the same as it does for other apps. That backup goes to your iCloud

account or your computer, under Apple's control, not mine. I have no access to

it. You can turn this off for Notebook in **Settings → [Your Name] → iCloud →

Manage Storage → Backups**.

Deleting your writing

Deleting the app from your device deletes its file and everything in it. There

is no copy anywhere else, so this cannot be undone.

Children

Notebook does not collect data from anyone, including children.

Changes to this policy

If a future version of Notebook does something different with your writing,

this page will be updated before that version is released.
